newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda says its army killed 60 Sudanese troops.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says its army killed 60 Sudanese troops.

text.p: Uganda said on Friday its army killed 60 Sudanese soldiers and captured more than 100 just inside Uganda, beating back a joint attack on Monday by the Sudanese army and Ugandan rebels.

Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi in a statement published by the state-owned New Vision daily denied a report from state Sudan radio that 306 Ugandan soldiers were killed the same day in a battle south of the south Sudanese capital Juba.
He said Uganda's army on Monday repulsed an attack by Sudanese troops and Ugandan Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) rebels at Lelabur just inside the northern Ugandan side of the border with south Sudan.

"Sixty Sudanese armed forces were killed and 114 captured. The captives are in the custody of the fourth division in northern Uganda. Sixty-eight LRA bandits were killed and 50 were either captured or surrendered," he added.

He gave no Ugandan army casualties, except to say that two members of a special army unit tracking LRA leader Joseph Kony in south Sudan were missing and it was unclear if they were killed or captured.

In his statement he denied a report on state Sudan radio on Thursday quoting Sudan's army as saying 306 Ugandan soldiers were killed on Monday in a battle 70 km (44 miles) south of Juba as they attempted to attack the capital of south Sudan.

"On April 14 the UPDF (Uganda People's Defence Forces) attacked a combined force of about two companies of Sudan forces and two companies of Kony bandits near Lelabur just inside the Uganda-Sudan border," Mbabazi said.

"This combined force had the intention of establishing a base in Gulu or Kitgum (in Uganda) for purposes of carrying out intelligence work in preparation for an offensive by the Sudanese armed forces and Kony bandits in northern Uganda."
"The full names and particulars of especially the captives will be availed to the public in due course," he added. A Ugandan army spokesman said on Friday he had nothing to add to the statement.
Mbabazi said the Ugandan army captured an assortment of arms and the Sudanese and Ugandan captives were being held in Gulu.
Khartoum accuses Ugandan troops of fighting alongside Sudanese rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) in south Sudan while Kampala accuses Sudan's army of aiding the LRA.
Forces under SPLA leader John Garang's command have stepped up their war this year to topple Khartoum's Islamist government in a rebel coalition called the National Democratic Alliance.
Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it aims to trigger a popular uprising in Khartoum.
The SPLA said last week its forces had overrun a major base of the LRA in south Sudan as part of its push on Juba but denied this meant it was fighting on behalf of Uganda's government.
